tech.name: OpenAI dots (always-on ChatGPT agents)
tech.status: shipped, rolling out: Pro and Business Premium in eligible markets; Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare beta when an admin enables it
tech.one_line: Always-on ChatGPT agents, each on its own cloud computer, that work toward your goals in the background (read-only), learn from feedback and ask before sensitive actions.

predecessor.name: A ChatGPT chat and ChatGPT agent mode (2025): one task per request, then it waits

hook.text: OpenAI dots: before, your ChatGPT would stop, wait for you; now your dot works 24/7, but how, at what risk, in 60 seconds?

claims.text: A ChatGPT agent task starts when you describe it, and ChatGPT notifies you when it's done with your task.
A dot can work towards your goals 24/7.
Dots use auto-review and Custom Rules (allow, require approval, block) for actions that could affect your accounts or share information.

before.text: Here's how, in one shop you run. Old ChatGPT, even 2025's agent mode, was the clerk at the counter: you ring, it does that one task, then waits for the next ring. Go home, and no new work starts.

claims.text: ChatGPT agent (July 17, 2025) does work for you using its own virtual computer.
In agent mode you select it in the composer and describe your desired task.
ChatGPT agent sends a notification when it's done with your task.

new.text: Now a dot works the night shift. It has its own desk, a cloud computer, and your goals pinned on the wall. While you're away, it reads your connected apps, but it can't send a thing.

claims.text: Dots were announced at DevDay and rolled out in ChatGPT on September 29, 2026.
DevDay 2026 was on September 29, 2026.
Each dot works on its own cloud computer, with its own browser and the apps you've connected.
A dot knows your goals and standards and can work towards your goals 24/7.
When you aren't actively working with it, your dot looks for ways to help in the background (proactive research).
Proactive research uses tools restricted to be read-only: they can't send messages, change app content, or control your browser or computer.

why.text: Morning, a note: you forgot an invoice; it's ready; send it? You tap yes. Say "shorter notes", and it learns. And changing a password always stays with you.

claims.text: An early tester's dot noticed he'd forgotten to invoice a publication, prepared the invoice, and sent it after his approval.
Dots can message you with progress, questions, or decisions that need you.
Dots learn from feedback over time and learn your preferences.
Certain sensitive tasks, such as changing a password, always stay with you.

takeaway.text: How? Its own computer, working toward your goals. What risk? Away, it only reads; it asks before sensitive steps. It still makes mistakes, so check its work. The shop never closes now, but the keys are still yours.

claims.text: Each dot works on its own cloud computer and works towards your goals.
Background proactive research is read-only.
Custom Rules can require approval; auto-review checks actions that could affect your accounts or share information.
Dots can still make mistakes, so always review consequential work.

background.text: Dots look like little floating cartoon dots; much of this was already possible through Codex and agent harnesses.
